title: CHA2DS2-VASc score
purpose: Estimate annual ischaemic stroke risk in non-valvular atrial fibrillation to guide oral anticoagulation.

items.label: Vascular disease (prior MI, PAD, aortic plaque)

scoring.notes: Age contributes either 1 (65–74) or 2 (≥75), not both.

references.label: ESC Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation

title: HAS-BLED bleeding risk score
purpose: Estimate 1-year major bleeding risk in patients with atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation; flag modifiable risk factors.

interpretation.action: Caution and regular review; address modifiable factors. Not a reason to withhold anticoagulation alone.

references.label: ESC atrial fibrillation guidelines

title: Wells score for deep vein thrombosis
purpose: Estimate pre-test probability of lower-limb DVT to guide D-dimer and imaging.

items.label: Active cancer (treatment within 6 months or palliative)
Paralysis, paresis or recent plaster immobilisation of leg
Recently bedridden ≥3 days or major surgery within 12 weeks
Localised tenderness along deep venous system
Calf swelling >3 cm vs asymptomatic side
Pitting oedema confined to symptomatic leg
Alternative diagnosis at least as likely as DVT

references.label: Wells PS et al.; NICE venous thromboembolic diseases guideline

title: Wells score for pulmonary embolism
purpose: Estimate pre-test probability of pulmonary embolism to guide D-dimer and CT pulmonary angiography.

items.label: Clinical signs and symptoms of DVT
PE is the most likely diagnosis
Immobilisation ≥3 days or surgery within 4 weeks

interpretation.action: D-dimer; if negative, PE excluded (consider PERC in low-risk).

references.label: Wells PS et al.; NICE venous thromboembolic diseases guideline

title: PERC rule (Pulmonary Embolism Rule-out Criteria)
purpose: In patients already assessed as low pre-test probability, exclude PE without D-dimer if all 8 criteria are negative.

items.label: No recent trauma or surgery (within 4 weeks)

scoring.notes: PERC-negative = ALL 8 criteria satisfied. Only valid when clinical gestalt is already low-risk.

interpretation.action: PE can be excluded without D-dimer.
Cannot rule out PE on PERC; pursue D-dimer/imaging per pathway.

references.label: Kline JA et al. PERC rule

title: National Early Warning Score 2
purpose: Standardised bedside track-and-trigger score to detect and respond to acute clinical deterioration in adults.

items.label: SpO2 (Scale 1 or Scale 2 for hypercapnic risk)

scoring.notes: Each parameter scores 0–3 by physiological band; confusion/new ACVPU change scores 3.

interpretation.action: Emergency assessment by critical-care-competent team; consider transfer to higher care.

references.label: Royal College of Physicians, NEWS2

title: Glasgow Coma Scale
purpose: Assess and track depth of impaired consciousness; component of trauma and neurological assessment.

items.label: Eye opening (E): spontaneous 4, to sound 3, to pressure 2, none 1
Verbal response (V): orientated 5, confused 4, words 3, sounds 2, none 1
Motor response (M): obeys 6, localises 5, normal flexion 4, abnormal flexion 3, extension 2, none 1

scoring.notes: Report components (e.g. E3V4M5) as well as total; record best response and any untestable component.

interpretation.action: Close monitoring; imaging and senior review.
Airway at risk — consider intubation; urgent critical-care/neurosurgical input.

references.label: Teasdale & Jennett; GCS structured assessment

title: Centor score (McIsaac modification)
purpose: Estimate likelihood of group A streptococcal pharyngitis to guide testing and antibiotics.

interpretation.action: Consider rapid antigen test; antibiotics only if positive.
Test and treat if positive; FeverPAIN is an alternative tool.

references.label: McIsaac WJ et al.; national sore throat guidance

title: Ottawa ankle rules
purpose: Identify which acute ankle/midfoot injuries require radiography, safely reducing unnecessary X-rays.

items.label: Bone tenderness at posterior edge/tip of lateral malleolus
Bone tenderness at posterior edge/tip of medial malleolus
Bone tenderness at base of 5th metatarsal
Inability to bear weight (4 steps) both immediately and in ED

scoring.notes: Ankle X-ray if malleolar-zone pain plus malleolar tenderness or inability to weight-bear; foot X-ray if midfoot pain plus navicular/5th-MT tenderness or inability to weight-bear.

references.label: Stiell IG et al. Ottawa ankle rules

title: Ottawa knee rules
purpose: Identify which acute knee injuries require radiography.

items.label: Inability to bear weight (4 steps) both immediately and in ED

references.label: Stiell IG et al. Ottawa knee rules

title: Alvarado score for acute appendicitis
purpose: Estimate likelihood of acute appendicitis to support triage and imaging decisions.

interpretation.action: Consider discharge with review or alternative diagnosis.

references.label: Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis

title: Child-Pugh score for cirrhosis severity
purpose: Grade severity of chronic liver disease and estimate prognosis; informs surgical risk and management.

scoring.notes: Each parameter scores 1–3.

references.label: Pugh RNH et al.

title: MELD score (Model for End-stage Liver Disease)
purpose: Predict 3-month mortality in chronic liver disease; used for transplant prioritisation.

scoring.notes: Calculated from a logarithmic formula of bilirubin, creatinine, INR (and sodium for MELD-Na); not a simple sum.

interpretation.action: Close monitoring; transplant discussion as indicated.

references.label: Kamath PS et al.; UNOS allocation

title: Padua prediction score for VTE risk
purpose: Stratify hospitalised medical patients for venous thromboembolism risk to guide thromboprophylaxis.

references.label: Barbar S et al. Padua prediction score

title: Apgar score
purpose: Rapid assessment of newborn condition at 1 and 5 minutes after birth.

items.label: Activity (muscle tone): active 2, some flexion 1, limp 0

scoring.notes: Assess at 1 and 5 minutes (and every 5 min if <7); not a predictor of long-term outcome and not used alone to guide resuscitation.

interpretation.action: Stimulate, support; follow neonatal resuscitation algorithm.

references.label: Apgar V; AAP/AHA neonatal resuscitation

title: CURB-65 severity score for community-acquired pneumonia
purpose: Assess severity of community-acquired pneumonia to guide site of care.

scoring.notes: CRB-65 omits urea for community settings without bloods.

interpretation.action: Admit; assess for critical care, especially score 4–5.

references.label: Lim WS et al.; BTS community-acquired pneumonia guideline

title: HEART score for major adverse cardiac events
purpose: Risk-stratify chest pain in the emergency department for 6-week major adverse cardiac events (MACE).

items.label: ECG (normal / non-specific repolarisation / significant ST deviation)

scoring.notes: Each component scores 0-2.

interpretation.action: Admit for observation and serial troponin.

references.label: Six AJ et al. HEART score

title: TIMI risk score for UA/NSTEMI
purpose: Estimate 14-day risk of adverse outcomes in unstable angina / NSTEMI.

references.label: Antman EM et al. TIMI risk score

title: ABCD2 score for stroke risk after TIA
purpose: Estimate short-term stroke risk after a transient ischaemic attack.

interpretation.action: Urgent TIA-clinic assessment regardless; modern pathways assess all TIAs urgently.

references.label: Johnston SC et al. ABCD2 score; NICE stroke/TIA guidance

title: 4Ts score for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
purpose: Estimate the probability of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT).

items.label: Timing of platelet fall (5-10 days / >10 days etc.)
oTher cause of thrombocytopenia (none evident scores higher)

scoring.notes: Each of the 4 Ts scores 0-2.

interpretation.action: HIT unlikely; usually no need to stop heparin on this basis alone.
Send HIT antibody testing; consider stopping heparin and using a non-heparin anticoagulant.
Stop all heparin, start a non-heparin anticoagulant, confirm with testing.

references.label: Lo GK et al. 4Ts score

title: Westley croup severity score
purpose: Grade severity of croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) in children.

interpretation.action: Single dose of dexamethasone; usually safe for home.
Dexamethasone, observe; nebulised adrenaline if needed.
Nebulised adrenaline + steroids; close monitoring, anticipate airway support.

references.label: Westley CR et al. croup score

title: Glasgow-Imrie score for acute pancreatitis severity
purpose: Predict severity of acute pancreatitis at 48 hours.

scoring.notes: Mnemonic PANCREAS; assessed within 48 h.

interpretation.action: Consider HDU/ICU; aggressive monitoring and support.

references.label: Blamey SL et al. Glasgow-Imrie criteria

title: Rockall score for upper GI bleeding
purpose: Estimate rebleeding and mortality risk after upper gastrointestinal bleeding (full score includes endoscopy).

items.label: Stigmata of recent haemorrhage at endoscopy

scoring.notes: Pre-endoscopy (clinical) Rockall uses the first three variables.

interpretation.action: Low rebleed/mortality risk; early discharge may be considered.
Admit; the higher the score, the greater the rebleed/mortality risk.

references.label: Rockall TA et al. risk scoring after UGIB

title: Revised Geneva score for pulmonary embolism
purpose: Estimate clinical probability of pulmonary embolism (objective alternative to Wells).

items.label: Pain on lower-limb deep venous palpation and unilateral oedema

references.label: Le Gal G et al. revised Geneva score

title: AUDIT-C alcohol use screen
purpose: Brief screen for hazardous or harmful alcohol use.

items.label: How often do you have a drink containing alcohol? (0-4)
How many drinks on a typical drinking day? (0-4)
How often do you have >=6 drinks on one occasion? (0-4)

interpretation.action: Brief intervention; full AUDIT if indicated.

references.label: Bush K et al. AUDIT-C; WHO AUDIT

title: Caprini score for surgical VTE risk
purpose: Stratify venous thromboembolism risk in surgical patients to guide prophylaxis.

items.label: Multiple weighted risk factors (age, BMI, prior VTE, thrombophilia, malignancy, surgery type, immobility, etc.)

scoring.notes: Each risk factor contributes 1-5 points; see the full Caprini factor list.

interpretation.action: Early mobilisation; mechanical prophylaxis as appropriate.
Pharmacological prophylaxis (unless contraindicated) +/- mechanical; consider extended duration.

references.label: Caprini JA. Thrombosis risk assessment

title: Light's criteria for pleural exudate
purpose: Classify a pleural effusion as exudate or transudate.

items.label: Pleural fluid LDH > 2/3 upper limit of normal serum LDH

scoring.notes: Exudate if ANY one criterion is met; otherwise transudate.

interpretation.action: Investigate for infection, malignancy, inflammation, PE.
Treat the systemic cause (heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome).

references.label: Light RW et al.; BTS pleural disease guideline

title: FIB-4 index for hepatic fibrosis
purpose: Non-invasive estimate of advanced hepatic fibrosis (e.g. in NAFLD/viral hepatitis).

scoring.notes: FIB-4 = (Age x AST) / (Platelets x sqrt(ALT)); not a simple sum.

references.label: Sterling RK et al. FIB-4 index

title: Sequential Organ Failure Assessment
purpose: Quantify organ dysfunction in critically ill patients; component of the Sepsis-3 definition.

scoring.notes: Each organ system scores 0-4; an acute rise of >=2 defines sepsis-related organ dysfunction (Sepsis-3).

interpretation.action: Escalate care; treat sepsis per bundle.

references.label: Vincent JL et al. SOFA; Singer M et al. Sepsis-3

title: Patient Health Questionnaire-9
purpose: Screen for and grade severity of depressive disorder over the past 2 weeks; can also track treatment response.

items.label: Little interest or pleasure in doing things (anhedonia)
Trouble falling/staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Feeling bad about yourself / a failure / let family down
Moving or speaking noticeably slowly, or restlessness/agitation
Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of self-harm

scoring.notes: Each item scored 0=not at all, 1=several days, 2=more than half the days, 3=nearly every day.

interpretation.action: Watchful waiting, sleep hygiene, low-intensity psychological intervention; reassess in 2–4 weeks.
Offer psychological therapy ± SSRI; safety-net for suicide risk.
Combine pharmacotherapy and psychological therapy; review weekly initially.
Urgent combined treatment; consider specialist referral or hospital admission if active suicidal ideation.

references.label: Kroenke et al. JGIM 2001; NICE Depression guideline

title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7
purpose: Screen for and grade severity of generalised anxiety disorder over the past 2 weeks.

items.label: Feeling nervous, anxious or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Being so restless it's hard to sit still
Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen

scoring.notes: Each item scored 0–3 over past 2 weeks.

interpretation.action: Combined pharmacotherapy + psychological therapy; consider specialist input.

references.label: Spitzer et al. Arch Intern Med 2006; NICE Anxiety guideline

title: Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol — revised
purpose: Quantify alcohol withdrawal severity and guide symptom-triggered benzodiazepine dosing.

scoring.notes: Reassess every 1–4 h; trend more important than absolute single score.

interpretation.action: Supportive only; reassess at 2–4 h intervals.
Symptom-triggered benzodiazepine (e.g. diazepam 10 mg or lorazepam 2 mg per CIWA score).

interpretation.meaning: Severe withdrawal — risk of seizures and DTs
interpretation.action: Aggressive benzodiazepine loading; consider HDU; treat hypomagnesaemia, hypokalaemia; thiamine 200–500 mg IV; CT brain if focal signs.

references.label: Sullivan et al. Br J Addiction 1989; NICE alcohol use disorders guideline

title: Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale
purpose: Grade opioid withdrawal severity to guide induction onto buprenorphine and supportive treatment.

scoring.notes: Score before each buprenorphine induction dose.

interpretation.action: Symptomatic care; consider induction when ≥12 to avoid precipitated withdrawal.
Buprenorphine induction safe — start 2–4 mg sublingual and titrate.

references.label: Wesson DR, Ling W. J Psychoactive Drugs 2003; SAMHSA TIP 63

title: STOP-BANG questionnaire
purpose: Pre-test probability of obstructive sleep apnoea (especially before surgery / sedation).

interpretation.action: No further OSA evaluation needed unless symptomatic.
Refer for sleep study; consider postoperative monitored bed and avoid long-acting opioid sedation.

references.label: Chung et al. Anesthesiology 2008; ASA OSA practice guideline

title: Revised Cardiac Risk Index (Lee)
purpose: Estimate risk of major adverse cardiac events after non-cardiac surgery.

items.label: High-risk surgery (intraperitoneal, intrathoracic or suprainguinal vascular)

interpretation.action: Consider functional capacity, biomarker testing, anaesthetic plan.
Cardiology consult; consider further testing; high-dependency / ICU postoperatively.

references.label: Lee et al. Circulation 1999; ACC/AHA Perioperative guideline

title: Quick Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment
purpose: Bedside identification of patients with suspected infection at risk of poor outcomes outside ICU.

interpretation.action: Continue assessment; not a rule-out for sepsis.
Activate sepsis pathway (Sepsis Six); senior review; consider HDU.

references.label: Sepsis-3 — Singer et al. JAMA 2016

title: Mini-Mental State Examination
purpose: Bedside screen for cognitive impairment.

items.label: Attention and calculation (serial 7s or spelling WORLD backwards)

scoring.notes: Adjust interpretation for age and education.

interpretation.action: Reassure; if clinical suspicion persists use MoCA.
Dementia workup; support and safety planning.
Comprehensive geriatric / psychiatric assessment; capacity considerations.

references.label: Folstein et al. J Psychiatr Res 1975; NICE dementia guideline

title: Modified Bishop score
purpose: Assess cervical favourability for induction of labour.

interpretation.action: Use cervical ripening (PGE2, misoprostol, or balloon catheter) before oxytocin.
Either ripening or direct oxytocin induction acceptable.

references.label: Bishop EH. Obstet Gynecol 1964; ACOG induction guidance; WHO Recommendations on Induction of Labour

title: Full Outline of UnResponsiveness
purpose: Coma assessment in intubated patients; complements / replaces GCS in ICU.

scoring.notes: Captures key brainstem reflexes and respiratory pattern that GCS does not.

interpretation.action: Initiate brain death protocol per local criteria.
ICU level care, neuroimaging, address reversible causes.

references.label: Wijdicks et al. Ann Neurol 2005
